nodes.title: READ ME - ALPHA-T1
widgets_values:
# ALPHA-T1  -  single-pass MiniMax H3 i2v

The whole thing in one H3 pass. No LTX, no upscaler, no second sampler. This is the config
that rendered a 7 s clip at 704x384 in ~166 s with coherent motion and native audio.

## Use
1. Drop a still into **First frame**.
2. Write the prompt in H3's template (positive box shows the shape: one referenced first
   frame, ONE action with timed beats, an explicit camera contract, then soundscape).
3. Set **Duration** (seconds); the math node snaps it to H3's 17k+5 frame law at 24 fps.
4. **Resolution** = the only quality/speed dial. Turn it up for more pixels in the same
   single pass:
     - 0.27 MP = 704x384   (~166 s)  <- default, the fast one
     - 0.4  MP = 864x480
     - 0.6  MP = 1056x576
     - 0.98 MP = 1344x768  (H3's ceiling)
5. Queue. Output lands in `output/video/ALPHA-T1/` as mp4 with audio.

## Baked in (leave alone)
euler + bong_tangent, **12 steps**, CFG 1, turbo LoRA @ 0.5, FusedModulation + Sol-Attn
(tau 1.3, min_tokens 4096, exact_kv). Seed is fixed at 757358688076805 - randomize it for
variety.

The lesson from the SA / LTX experiments: the motion and composition are entirely in this
one pass. A second pass (LTX refine or H3 2x upscale) only adds pixels, and costs far more
than just turning the resolution dial here.

detailed_description:
The target video is a premium cinematic horror title sequence in a restrained abstract audiovisual style. The frame remains a locked 16:9 composition with deep blacks, precise ivory typography, fine photochemical grain, and controlled warm-amber and cold-blue-white signal light.

[Shot 1] The video begins on a pure black frame. During the opening high-string rise in <Audio 1>, an extremely faint amber horizontal trace becomes visible at frame-left while a nearly imperceptible cold rain texture gathers at frame-right. The center remains dark and empty, creating one full second of visual tension after the preceding drag-away scene.

At the first strong musical impact in <Audio 1>, within the first second, the small red sync point ignites at the exact center of frame. The impact sends a warm amber waveform from frame-left toward the red point. At the same instant, a cold blue-white signal erupts from the point toward frame-right, combining an audio waveform, restrained lightning filaments, and rain streaks. The two signals remain parts of one continuous horizontal energy line, with the warm Foley world visibly transforming into the cold film world at the red sync point.

At 00:01.200, the complete word BACKLOT appears at center as a single clean exposure reveal, its full ivory condensed letterforms already formed and perfectly stable. Beneath it, A LIMINAL FRAMES PRODUCTION appears as one complete, smaller, widely tracked line. The full visible typography reads exactly:
BACKLOT
A LIMINAL FRAMES PRODUCTION

From 00:01.500 through 00:04.800, both lines remain crisp and continuously readable. The camera stays locked. The amber waveform breathes with small amplitude to the rhythm of <Audio 1>; the central red point pulses subtly on musical accents; the blue-white waveform travels gently while rain moves downward and occasional lightning energy flickers within the cold side. Signal motion remains behind and around the lettering while the type holds still.

At 00:04.800, all movement gradually settles. The waveforms, rain, red sync point, calibration ticks, title scale, spacing, and lighting converge precisely toward <Picture 1>. The shot ends exactly on <Picture 1> as the literal final frame, preserving every pixel-level design relationship and the complete readable title card.
